synth.diagnosis:
VERDICT: a small-move Running Up row gets no positive evaluation for three reasons. The platform never evaluates the alert itself. The one evaluation it has for the name is off the row and taken at the wrong moment. And in the desk's usual data state that evaluation cannot pass. Move size is not the cause.

(1) NOTHING EVALUATIVE ON THE ROW.
- fillAlertCard (src/momentum_platform/dashboard/web/app.js:1028-1076) renders only Time, PM%/Day%, Symbol+flame+session, Price and Strategy.
- A click only selects the symbol (app.js:1076).
- The per-condition reasons sit in alertDetail (app.js:1129), which only the timeline card can open.
- One note (app.js:16-18) describes the running_up rule, but the same tile also shows both squeezes. Those have no VWAP, fresh-high or leg rule, only a 5-min volume floor (momentum_events.py:200-207).

(2) THE EVALUATION THAT EXISTS IS ELSEWHERE.
- It is the server cascade, run for every desk symbol on its CURRENT metrics at the end of each build (session_builder.py:520-534).
- Only first-pullback plans are evaluated at their own bar (session_builder.py:378-385).
- The alert payload carries no cascade field (session_builder.py:412-431).

(3) THAT CASCADE FAILS CLOSED ON MISSING DATA.
- Amendment A5 kills below PILLARS_MIN = 4 (cascade.py:123) and counts an unknown float or catalyst as not passed (cascade.py:316-330).
- The catalyst pillar is `bool(i.catalyst_today or i.live_theme)` (cascade.py:323). It ignores catalyst_source_ok, although the catalyst gate itself reads UNKNOWN when there is no headline source (cascade.py:293-298). That gate was changed by A2 because 'the kill had been deciding on an absence of data, not an absence of news' (cascade.py:95-101).
- Replay at the alert bar over 174,920 tile rows: 0 non-REJECT. 95.7% are REJECT on pillars and 4.3% REJECT on price (scratchpad runup_study/analysis_full.txt §B).
- Assuming a verified float under 20M and a catalyst: REVIEW 44.6%, WAIT 19.7%, REJECT still-rising 17.0%, WATCH 8.4%, REJECT pillars 6.0%, REJECT price 4.3% (§D).
- A5 is preregistered (docs/preregistration.md:498-513). But FILTERS.md Layer 1 has no pillar count (knowledge-base/strategies/FILTERS.md:47-56) and calls RVOL ≥5× a dial (FILTERS.md:20, 218), and FILTERS.md wins threshold conflicts.

(4) THE WORKING INTERPRETATION IS HALF RIGHT.
- True: the trigger is 3% in 10 min (momentum_events.py:302), and 42.5% of tile rows are moves under 5% (extra_stats.txt).
- False as stated: these names are not unevaluated. Every alerting name is a desk name with a server verdict; that verdict just never reaches the row and cannot be positive.
- Missed: 14,435 of 143,864 running_up events (10.0%) are consolidated under HOD Momentum. 12,090 of them leave no Running Up row for that name in the next 10 min, because the leg is recorded (momentum_events.py:430) before the router suppresses the event (notify.py:199-213; analysis_full.txt §A).

(5) SMALL MEANS LOWER AMPLITUDE, NOT LOWER MEAN. Gross, no costs (analysis_full.txt §C):
- move 3-4%: median 30-min change −0.68%, mean −0.19%
- move 10%+: median −2.72%, mean +0.09%

(6) WHAT DOES MEASURE: THREE BAR-ONLY FEATURES. The grade uses alert-bar range, move and day change, as train 2016-23 percentiles.
- RTH 2024-26 test AUC10 is 0.725, day-clustered CI [0.716, 0.737].
- Quintile 1 reached +10% within 30 min 4.7% of the time, quintile 5 40.2%.
- But quintile 5's median 30-min change is −4.1% and its median dip is −4.0% (runup_study/merge_checks2.txt).
- Net R of passing first-pullback plans is negative in every decile of the published score, −0.39 to −0.63 on test (results.txt).

So the fix is an honest evaluation on the row, not a positive verdict:
- unknown inputs shown as 'verify'
- measured kills shown as kills
- an amplitude grade with its risk next to it

Paper only; no edge is claimed (CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-regime-filter.md). Scratch outputs from this task: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-day-trading-bot/6b4cf148-a65f-567e-98fc-7d02cdbb6f60/scratchpad/runup_study/merge_checks.txt and merge_checks2.txt (scripts merge_checks.py, merge_checks2.py, merge_checks_lib.py). No repo file was modified.

# Running Up: how an alert is made, what is shown, and how the name is evaluated

**Verdict.** A Running Up row has no evaluation attached to it. The tile shows five fields. The only real evaluation is the server cascade, and three things stop it from being positive. It runs on every desk name for the current moment, not at the alert. It is shown only on the verdict card, when the owner clicks the name. In the desk's usual data state (float unknown, no catalyst dated today) it cannot pass: the pillar gate needs 4/5 and the count stops at 3/5. In a 10-year replay, 0 of 174,920 tile rows got a non-REJECT verdict.

**Testing the working interpretation against the code:**
- **"Fires on small moves": true.** The threshold is 3% in 10 minutes. In the replay, 42.5% of tile rows were moves under 5%.
- **"Names the platform does not evaluate at all": false as stated.**
  - Every alerting name is already a desk name.
  - Every desk name has a pillar row on the board and a server verdict.
  - That evaluation is not on the alert, is not taken at alert time, and fails closed on missing data.
- **"A real runner shows no positive evaluation because inputs are missing": true.** It is structural.
- **One gap the interpretation missed:** about 10% of Running Up legs never reach the tile at all (consolidation, section 1 step 5).

---

## 1. How an alert is produced

| step | where | what happens |
|---|---|---|
| Universe | `ibkr_desk.py:842-870` | Records, and so scanners, exist only for `self.symbols`. |
| Desk admission | `ibkr_desk.py:975-992`, `1026-1040`; `ibkr_scanner.py:242`; `config/desk-profile.json:15-21` | IBKR scan union, kept if `change_pct >= minGainPct` (10) in $1–30. Desk capped at `maxSymbols: 8`. No eviction code: names leave only on a data-permission or contract error (`:400-447`). |
| Rebuild | `ibkr_desk.py:908-912`; `desk-profile.json:23` | The whole session since 04:00 is rebuilt every `rebuildSeconds: 3` with a fresh engine and router. `volume_floor_scale=1.0`. |
| Forming minute | `session_builder.py:234-261`; `scripts/desk_replay.py:5-9` | 10-second candles are aggregated into minutes, including the minute still forming. |
| Scanner list and order | `session_builder.py:279-293` | `FivePillarsAlert`, `HodMomentumScanner`, `UptrendScanner`, `RunningMoveScanner(down)`, `squeeze_5_in_5()`, `squeeze_10_in_10()`, `Breakout52wScanner`, then the list scanners. One `engine.process` per minute bar (`:357-365`). |
| Engine → router | `engine.py:32-46` | Every event goes to `router.handle`. No `store=`, so nothing is persisted. |
| Router order | `notify.py:165-231` | Severity → idempotency → cooldown → consolidation → fan-out. |
| Cooldown | `notify.py:117-131`, `181-197` | Key is `symbol\|scanner\|branch`. running_up and the two squeezes: 120 s. Cooldown is overridden by a price advance of ≥2%. Because the branch is in the key, a change between `uptrend_10m` and `uptrend_10m_hod` skips the cooldown. |
| Consolidation | `notify.py:132`, `199-213` | A same-symbol alert within 3.0 s of a delivered alert is suppressed as `consolidated_under_<primary>`. All scanners share the bar's `scan_ts`, and the list order puts `five_pillars_alert` and `hod_momentum` first. So a running_up on the same bar as a HOD Momentum alert is not delivered as its own alert. |
| Payload | `session_builder.py:412-431`; `base.py:52-71`; `momentum_events.py:431-447` | `values`: last, change_pct, rvol, rvol_5m, volume_5m, float_m, float_quality, gap_pct, hod_distance_pct, plus `reference_price`, `window_minutes`, `window_high`, `vwap_window`. Also `reasons` (each condition with pass/fail), `news`, `group`, `severity`, `branch`. **No cascade field.** |

### Which class carries `running_up`
It is **`UptrendScanner`**: it sets `scanner_id = "running_up"` and version 3.2.0 (`momentum_events.py:299-321`). `RunningMoveScanner` is instantiated only as `running_down` (`session_builder.py:285`) and as the two squeezes (`momentum_events.py:452-465`).

### The three scanners that feed the tile

| | `running_up` (UptrendScanner 3.2.0) | `squeeze_5_in_5` / `squeeze_10_in_10` (RunningMoveScanner) |
|---|---|---|
| move | ≥3.0% vs the close of the newest bar at least 10 min old (`:301-302`, `354-358`, `374`) | ≥5% in 5 min / ≥10% in 10 min (`:454`, `462`) |
| fresh high | the window high was printed in the last 3 min (`:360-361`, `375`) | none |
| right now | the current bar makes the window high or closes within 0.5% of it, **and is not red** (`:365-370`) | none |
| control | last ≥ 10-minute bar VWAP of closes (`:362-363`, `377`) | none |
| liquidity | `volume_5m ≥ 25,000` **or** ≥3 pillars by `pillars_passed` (`:27-47`, `364`) | `volume_5m ≥ 25,000` only, unscaled default (`:176`, `207`; `session_builder.py:286`) |
| price | ≥ $1 (`:305`) | ≥ $1 (`:177`) |
| at HOD | not a gate since 3.1.0; recorded only as branch `uptrend_10m_hod` (`:253-268`, `381`, `442`) | — |
| re-arm | once per leg: needs a non-higher-high minute since the last alert and a price ≥1% above it. The memory resets when the last alert is older than the 10-min window (`:411-430`) | `EdgeTracker(rearm_after_fails=3)`, i.e. 3 non-qualifying minutes on the desk (`:187`; `base.py:103-123`) |
| severity | `high` if the move is ≥6% (2×threshold), else `medium` (`:441`) | always `medium` |

## 2. What the owner sees per alert
- **Tile** (`app.js:1019-1071`). Columns are Time, PM%/Day% (change from previous close, not the triggering move), Symbol with flame and PM/RTH/AH pill, Price, and Strategy label (`:1029-1036`, `1045-1066`).
  - Not shown: the 10-minute move, severity, RVOL, float, pillar score, verdict.
  - Only primary scanner IDs are listed (`loggedAlerts`, `:201-203`), capped at 80 rows (`:1021`).
  - The rows come from a browser-side log keyed by `symbol|scanner|branch|second` (`:173-200`; `models.py:137-142`).
- **Tile note** (`app.js:17`). It describes only the running_up rule ("≥3% in 10 min · fresh 10-min high · above VWAP · liquid. One alert per leg."). It does not mention the "not red, at window high" condition, and it does not apply to the two squeeze scanners shown in the same tile (`:18`).
- **Per-condition detail** (`alertDetail`, `app.js:1120-1143`). Reached only from the Alert timeline card (`:1074-1105`), not from the tile. A consolidated running_up appears only as "+N more" there (`:1087`, `1131-1134`).
- **Clicking a tile row** only selects the symbol (`app.js:1067`, `1954-1962`). Sound and tile flash fire on new arrivals (`:1987-2027`).

## 3. What evaluation exists, and for which names
- **Server cascade, every desk symbol, at the end of each build, using current metrics** (`session_builder.py:520-534`, which uses `meta["metrics"]` via `:610-615`).
  - Inputs carry no alert or momentum field (`cascade.py:135-165`).
  - The pillar gate needs ≥4 of price, gain ≥10, RVOL ≥5, float <20M, catalyst (`cascade.py:122-123`, `309-330`).
  - Float and catalyst only flag on their own (`:101`, `122`). Unknown counts as not passed.
- **Verdict card, selected symbol only** (`app.js:1679-1860`).
  - The verdict word is the server's (`:1734-1736`).
  - The "HOD / Running: ACTIVE" row (300 s after an alert, `:1686-1688`, `1849-1850`) and the "No live momentum event" wait (`:1723`) feed only the browser fallback verdict. An alert can never make the verdict positive.
- **Five Pillars board: every desk symbol** (`app.js:1176-1179`, `1226`).
- **Five Pillars list: only names passing price, gain and RVOL** (`five_pillars.py:177-179`), plus browser-added names with ≥3/5 (`app.js:819-831`).
- **First-pullback plans** are armed by the detector on every bar regardless of alerts (`session_builder.py:370-410`). No code in `src/` consumes `running_up` outside the scanner, router and session builder.

**Can a Running Up alert bring a name onto the desk or into the cascade?** No. Alerts exist only for names already on the desk, and the cascade runs on those names whether or not they alert.

## 4. What is stored about alerts
- **Nothing durable.** The ledger schema (`src/journal/ledger.py:70-251`) has decisions, board_snapshots, orders, decision_revisions, quote_ticks, risk_day, order_events, halts, bars, bars_10s, quotes, exercise_state, candidates and actuals. There is no alerts table.
- `EventStore.scanner_events` exists (`store.py:18-36`) but only the CLI uses it (`cli.py:66-67`, `89-96`), not the desk.
- `/api/v1/scanner-events` serves the in-memory frames (`server.py:408-409`). `scripts/alerts.py:12-13` says the list is empty once the desk stops.

## 5. Replay check (mechanics, not edge)
I ran the desk's own event scanners and RouterConfig, in the same order, over all 2,608 cached SIP days (2016-02-03 → 2026-08-21). For each event I evaluated the cascade at the alert bar, the way plans are evaluated at `session_builder.py:378-385`. Scripts and outputs are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-day-trading-bot/6b4cf148-a65f-567e-98fc-7d02cdbb6f60/scratchpad/runup_study/`: `replay_alerts.py`, `analyze.py`, `analysis_full.txt`, `extra_stats.txt`.

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| tile-visible rows | 174,920 (running_up 128,960 · 5in5 35,836 · 10in10 10,124) |
| moves under 5% | 42.5% of tile rows; 57.7% of running_up rows |
| day change under 10% at the alert | 8.6% |
| cascade at alert, float unknown and no news | REJECT on pillars 95.7%, REJECT on price 4.3%, **non-REJECT 0** |
| same cascade, assuming float verified <20M and a catalyst today | REVIEW 44.6% · WAIT 19.7% · REJECT on still-rising 17.0% · WATCH 8.4% · REJECT on pillars 6.0% · REJECT on price 4.3% |
| running_up hidden by consolidation | 14,435 of 143,864 emitted (10.0%), all under hod_momentum |
| of those, no Running Up row for that name in the next 10 min | 12,090 — the scanner records the alert at `:430` before the router drops it, so that leg is used up |
| rows per symbol-day | median 6, p90 27, max 81 |
| rows by time (ET) | 04–07: 9.7% · 07–09:30: 23.3% · 09:30–11:30: 35.7% · after 11:30: 31.2% |

Forward 30 minutes from the alert bar's close. This is gross, has no entry rule, no stop and no costs, so it is not a trade and not a claim of edge.

| cohort | n | median ret30 | mean ret30 | median MFE / MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| move 3–4% | 46,333 | −0.68% | −0.19% | 2.73 / −3.23% |
| move 10%+ | 28,793 | −2.72% | +0.09% | 7.62 / −8.84% |
| day change 0–10% | 9,534 (2,922 + 6,612) | +0.20 / +0.27% | +1.70 / +1.74% | ~3.0 / ~−2.7% |
| day change 50%+ | 56,236 | −2.50% | −0.85% | 5.75 / −7.35% |
| gain ≥10 and RVOL ≥5 | 65,735 | −1.80% | −0.80% | 4.33 / −5.67% |
| neither gain ≥10 nor RVOL ≥5 | 10,610 | +0.33% | +1.92% | 3.25 / −2.72% |
| first tile row of the symbol-day | 16,823 | −0.36% | +1.35% | 4.24 / −4.18% |
| later tile rows | 150,553 | −1.39% | −0.38% | 4.06 / −5.08% |
| running_up at HOD | 6,237 | −0.27% | +1.05% | 4.33 / −3.93% |
| running_up below HOD | 116,492 | −1.17% | −0.28% | 3.65 / −4.50% |

What this shows:
- Small moves are mainly lower amplitude, not lower mean.
- On this crude measure, the two pillars the desk can measure rank alerts the wrong way round.
- A first leg differs from its repeats; the tile does not mark which is which.

**Replay limits:**
- No float or news (`float_provenance` is "unavailable" on all 25,716 rows).
- RVOL is the daily measure, with no time-of-day profile, so it is understated pre-market.
- Average daily volume is approximated as `prior_dollar_volume_20d / prev_close`.
- Complete minutes only.
- Each day replays all of its candidates, not an 8-name desk.

## 6. Why a small-move alert carries no positive evaluation
1. **Not on the row.** The tile renders no verdict, pillar count, move %, RVOL or float, even though the payload carries most of them (`app.js:1029-1066`; `base.py:52-71`).
2. **Structurally REJECT.** With float unknown or a share-count bound over 20M, and no catalyst dated today, the pillar count stops at 3/5, below the 4 required (`cascade.py:316-330`). IBKR fundamentals are often not entitled (`ibkr_desk.py:416-419`), so float is often missing.
3. **The pillar gate uses numbers that `FILTERS.md` treats as dials.** Its Layer 1 has no gain gate and no pillar count (`FILTERS.md:47-56`). It calls RVOL ≥5× "a scanner dial, not a gate", with a profitable floor of 1.5× (`:20`, `:162`, `:218`). The cascade's A5 count kills on both. CLAUDE.md says `FILTERS.md` wins threshold conflicts, so this needs a decision, and `FILTERS.md` does not record A5.
4. **Wrong moment.** The verdict is for the latest bar, not the alert minute (`session_builder.py:520-534`).
5. **Best legs routed away.** Running Up legs that coincide with HOD Momentum are filed under HOD and burn the leg (`notify.py:203-213`; `momentum_events.py:430`).
6. **Admission has no follow-up.** Names enter at ≥10% gain and are never re-checked. A faded name can alert on a 3% bounce while its day change is under 10%.

## 7. Evaluation gaps
- **G1. No verdict on the row.** No verdict, pillar score, triggering move, severity, RVOL or float in the tile (`app.js:1029-1066`). Per-condition reasons are only in the timeline (`:1120-1143`).
- **G2. Alert and verdict are not joined.** No cascade snapshot is taken at alert time; the verdict is current-state only (`session_builder.py:520-534`).
- **G3. The cascade fails closed on missing data.** Pillars max out at 3/5 without float and catalyst (`cascade.py:316-330`). Replay: 0 positive verdicts in the desk's common data state.
- **G4. Threshold conflict.** The pillar gate kills on gain ≥10% and RVOL ≥5×, which `FILTERS.md:20/47-56/162/218` does not gate on.
- **G5. Consolidation hides about 10% of Running Up legs** and uses up the leg (`notify.py:199-213` against `momentum_events.py:411-430`). This cuts against the owner's 3.1.0 decision to show every runner (`:253-268`).
- **G6. One tile, three rule sets, one note** (`app.js:16-18`). The squeezes have no VWAP, fresh-high, not-red or leg logic, and a strict 25k floor (`momentum_events.py:166-223`, `452-465`).
- **G7. Repeats are not marked.** Median 6 rows per symbol-day; the tile does not separate first leg from repeat (replay section E).
- **G8. No session-window cue.** 31.2% of rows come after 11:30 ET, outside `FILTERS.md:163-164`. The tile shows only a PM/RTH/AH pill (`app.js:1058-1061`).
- **G9. "Pillars" means two different counts.**
  - Scanner liquidity counts news within 24 h (`five_pillars.py:83`, `106-110`, `131-140`).
  - The cascade counts a catalyst dated today, with no roundup and no reaction headline (`session_builder.py:882-920`; `cascade.py:318-324`).
- **G10. No alert persistence** (ledger schema `:70-251`; `scripts/alerts.py:12-13`). Live alert quality cannot be measured afterwards; only a replay can.
- **G11. Ghost alerts (plausible, not measured).** Alerts fire on the forming minute (`session_builder.py:234-261`). The browser log keeps any key it has seen once (`app.js:185-199`), even if later rebuilds no longer emit it.
- **G12. The universe is the desk.** At most 8 names, admitted at ≥10%, with no eviction (`ibkr_desk.py:975-992`; `desk-profile.json:19`). Running Up never discovers a name, and rows under 10% on the day are faded desk names.
- **G13. Momentum is display-only in the verdict.** The card's ACTIVE row has no input to the server verdict (`cascade.py:135-165`; `app.js:1734-1736`, `1849-1850`).
- **G14. ## 10. What this implies for evaluating a Running Up alert

These are derived from §2–8. The rubric is **A** throughout. It is a description of his selection, to be measured on history, not a claim of edge.

**Prior measurement to respect.** The `research/momentum-replication/reports/README.md` index records two results:
- A 0–100 pillar score used as a basket weight lost to equal weight in 16 of 16 matched pairs (`2026-08-score-basket.md`).
- "Nothing predicts the upside (max r=0.19)" (`2026-08-strategy-v2.md`).

A corpus-shaped grade will show selection quality, not expectancy.

1. **Grade the name, not the pop.** The alert's 10-minute move is only the trigger. Grade what he reads on the row: change from close (≥10% pillar; he wants 40–75%+), rank among gainers (top 10 to consider, top 3 to trade), RVOL (≥5× pillar; 2.5 is "pretty low"), session volume, float band (<5M bright, 11–20M fading), price band, and news freshness.
   - A 3% alert on a name up 14% on the day is, in his words, "not really moving all that much".
   - The same 3% alert on the #1 gainer up 200% is how JEM, UPC and EHGO were found.
2. **Give the curl its own reading** (O, 2026 recaps). For a below-HOD alert, show:
   - the distance to the prior HOD or pre-market high (his target),
   - whether price is back above VWAP,
   - whether the MACD is back positive.
   Mark a below-HOD alert long after the HOD with the MACD still negative as "back side" (C/O streams), not as a candidate.
3. **Count alerts; don't add more of them.** His signal is repeated and stacked hits (C, yg5E [00:17:02], w97 [00:58:21]). The local tile's "one alert per leg" (rules 8 and 10 in the UptrendScanner docstring) suppresses exactly that count. A per-symbol counter across Running Up, both squeeze windows and HOD Momentum would keep the tile quiet while restoring the count.
4. **Show missing pillars as "verify", not as fails.** A blank float, a missing headline (flame lag of up to 5 minutes, theme substitution) and the morning RVOL bias should all read as "verify" (§8). This is the direct fix for "a real runner shows no positive evaluation".
5. **Hard rejects stay in FILTERS.md.** Price outside $2–20 (with the penny-theme exception), float over 20M, more than 25% off the pre-market high, and the split test are gates. The scanner is discovery only (SCANNERS.md header; FILTERS.md Layer 0).
6. **Context flags, not gates:**
   - the 07:00–10:00 window and :00/:30 news timing,
   - first move of the day vs a later leg,
   - foreign listing, a weak daily chart, "in the shadow of a big move".
   Each is a stated reason he passes; none has a threshold.

## A simple score built on train, tested on 2024–2026
I averaged the train percentiles of the top five features in train order: bar range, move size, % up on the day, % above VWAP and time of day (earlier is better). On the test years:
- **Ranking:** rank correlation with the 30-minute high is +0.317, and AUC10 is 0.693.
- **Top 10% vs bottom 10% of the score:**
  - Reached +10%: 49.5% vs 5.6%. The gap is +43.8 points, with a 95% interval of [+41.7, +45.8] when resampling by day.
  - Small moves: 20.1% vs 58.8%.
- **The catch, in the same deciles:**

  | Test, top vs bottom 10% | Top | Bottom |

  | Median change after 30 min | −4.5% | −0.4% |
  | Share higher after 30 min | 36.6% | 44.3% |
  | Net R of passing plans | −0.50 | −0.44 |

## Answer to "how could we make it better"
- **Grade every tile row with this score**, but call it a "follow-through / volatility grade", never a buy signal. It reliably flags the small-move noise; it does not find direction or edge.
- **Show the risk next to the grade.** The highest-graded alerts also have the deepest dips and the worst 30-minute close.
- **Dim weak alerts rather than hiding them.** Moves under 4% and alert bars under 1% range are the noisy group. The tile is a discovery layer, so it should not gate them.
- **Don't grade tile alerts with the pillar count.** It carries almost no signal here.
